method: manual parallel fan-out following anthropics/defending-code-reference-harness /vuln-scan methodology, scoped to the modules touched by vuln-001..vuln-018
focus_areas: Cross-cutting middleware, app wiring & dependencies (app.ts, middleware/*, package.json)
Frontend auth token handling & transaction rendering (authApi.ts, TransactionDetailPage.tsx)

findings.title: Passwords hashed with unsalted, unstretched SHA-256 instead of a password KDF
findings.description: hashPassword/verifyPassword use crypto.createHash('sha256') with no salt and no work factor. Identical passwords hash identically and SHA-256 is GPU-crackable at billions of candidates/sec.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker who reads the users table (DB leak, backup exposure) cracks passwordHash values via GPU hashcat in hours, then credential-stuffs other services.
findings.recommendation: Replace with bcrypt/scrypt/argon2id (salted, tunable work factor); rehash on next login.

findings.title: SQL injection in transaction description search via string-interpolated raw query
findings.description: searchTransactionsByDescription uses prisma.$queryRawUnsafe, splicing the untrusted `q` query-string param directly into `description ILIKE '%${q}%'`. No validate() middleware on this route.
findings.exploit_scenario: GET /transactions/search?q=' UNION SELECT ... -- returns other users' transaction rows or other table data via UNION SELECT.
findings.recommendation: Use $queryRaw tagged templates (auto-parameterized) instead of $queryRawUnsafe with interpolation.

findings.title: getTransactionById fetches any transaction by ID with no ownership check
findings.description: findUnique({ where: { id } }) has no filter tying the row to the caller's wallet, unlike listTransactions which correctly scopes via OR[senderWalletId, receiverWalletId].
findings.exploit_scenario: GET /transactions/{other-users-uuid} returns full counterparty/amount/status detail to an unrelated authenticated user.
findings.recommendation: findFirst({ where: { id, OR: [{senderWalletId: wallet.id},{receiverWalletId: wallet.id}] } }), NotFoundError on no match.

findings.title: Mass assignment via .passthrough() profile schema lets caller overwrite email/passwordHash/id
findings.description: updateProfileSchema uses .passthrough(); the validated body (with any extra keys) is spread directly into prisma.user.update's data object in users.service.ts.
findings.exploit_scenario: PATCH /api/users/me with {"passwordHash":"<attacker bcrypt hash>"} sets the account's password without the current-password check; {"email":...} hijacks the registered email with no verification.
findings.recommendation: Drop .passthrough(); whitelist mutable fields explicitly when building the Prisma update.

findings.title: Stored XSS via unsanitized transaction note rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.description: transaction.description (from sender-supplied transfer `note`, only trimmed/length-capped server-side) is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, bypassing React's auto-escaping.
findings.exploit_scenario: Sender sets note to ; payload executes in the viewer's browser when the transaction detail page is opened.
findings.recommendation: Render as plain JSX text ({transaction.description}); if HTML is genuinely needed, sanitize with DOMPurify and strip HTML server-side too.

findings.title: CORS reflects any Origin while allowing credentials
findings.description: cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }) reflects any caller's Origin instead of allowlisting env.CORS_ORIGIN, which is defined but unused for this purpose. Currently mitigated incidentally by httpOnly+SameSite cookies, not by the CORS layer itself.
findings.exploit_scenario: A cross-site page with credentials:'include' can read authenticated API responses if any factor weakens SameSite enforcement (webview quirks, future cookie change).
findings.recommendation: origin: (origin, cb) => cb(null, origin === env.CORS_ORIGIN), keep credentials:true only for that allowlisted origin.

findings.title: Transfer amount has no lower-bound/positivity check — negative amounts reverse the money flow
findings.description: createTransferSchema's amount has no .positive()/.min(). A negative amount inverts decrement/increment in transfers.service.ts and defeats the insufficient-balance guard (nothing is 'less than' a negative number).
findings.exploit_scenario: POST /transfers {"identifier":"<victim>","amount":-50000} credits the attacker and debits the victim, with any starting balance including zero.
findings.recommendation: Add .positive() to amount; defensively re-check amount > 0 in the service before use.
findings.note: Same schema line also lost the 2-decimal-place .refine() check (VULN-006, sub-cent precision drift) when vuln-005 and vuln-006 were merged onto security-testing — this scanner reported only the positivity gap and did NOT separately flag the missing precision check. Treat VULN-006 as a scan miss; see summary.

findings.title: Check-then-act balance validation with an injected delay enables a double-spend/overdraft race
findings.description: Balance is read via findUniqueOrThrow, checked, then (after an explicit 100ms sleep commented as 'fraud/velocity screening') decremented in a separate write — no atomic conditional update or row lock.
findings.exploit_scenario: N concurrent 100-unit transfers from a 100-unit balance all pass the check against the same stale read and all debit, driving the balance negative.
findings.recommendation: Use a single atomic conditional update (updateMany with balance gte filter, check affected count) instead of read-then-write.

findings.title: Dedicated auth rate limiter exists but is never applied to login/register
findings.description: authLimiter (10 req/15min) is defined but never imported anywhere; /register and /login only get the generic 300-req/15min apiLimiter.
findings.exploit_scenario: Up to 300 login attempts per IP per 15 minutes before any auth-specific throttle engages — practical credential stuffing, compounded by weak hashing and enumeration.
findings.recommendation: Apply authLimiter to /register and /login (and ideally /refresh).

findings.title: Password change does not revoke existing refresh tokens/sessions
findings.description: changePassword never calls revokeAllRefreshTokensForUser (which exists and is documented as being 'used on password change'); the handler only clears the caller's own cookies.
findings.exploit_scenario: A previously stolen refresh token keeps working via /auth/refresh even after the legitimate user changes their password specifically to lock the attacker out.
findings.recommendation: Call revokeAllRefreshTokensForUser(userId) inside changePassword after updating the hash.

findings.title: Access token additionally persisted to localStorage despite httpOnly-cookie session design
findings.description: Login/register responses also return accessToken in the JSON body (see F-AUTH-05, same root cause, backend side), and authApi.ts stores it in localStorage — directly readable by any script, unlike the httpOnly cookie the app otherwise relies on.
findings.exploit_scenario: Any XSS anywhere on the origin (e.g. F-FE-01) can read localStorage.getItem('payflow_access_token') and exfiltrate a portable bearer credential.
findings.recommendation: Remove the localStorage.setItem calls; rely solely on the httpOnly cookie.

findings.title: CSRF Origin-verification middleware exists but is never mounted anywhere
findings.description: verifyOrigin is fully implemented but not imported/app.use()'d in app.ts or any router. The only CSRF protection in production is the incidental SameSite-cookie behavior.
findings.exploit_scenario: If SameSite protection is ever weakened (proxy stripping Set-Cookie attributes, webview quirks, a future sameSite:'none' flow), cross-site mutating requests have no origin check to fall back on.
findings.recommendation: app.use(verifyOrigin) in app.ts after cookieParser, before routers.

findings.title: Global error handler leaks exception message and full stack trace to the client in all environments
findings.description: Non-ApiError exceptions are serialized with raw err.message/err.stack into the 500 JSON body with no isProduction/NODE_ENV gate.
findings.exploit_scenario: Any unhandled exception (type error, untranslated Prisma error) leaks internal file paths, line numbers, and dependency internals to the client.
findings.recommendation: Gate message/stack on isProduction; return a generic message and omit stack in production, keep server-side logging.

findings.title: Recipient lookup discloses other users' email, phone, and live wallet balance
findings.description: lookupRecipient returns email, phone, and walletBalance in addition to name/identifier — far more than a 'confirm transfer' UI needs.
findings.exploit_scenario: Any authenticated user enumerates phone/email against the lookup endpoint to confirm PayFlow accounts and harvest PII plus exact balances for targeted phishing.
findings.recommendation: Return only name and a masked identifier; drop email/phone/walletBalance from the DTO.

findings.title: Login endpoint distinguishes "no such account" from "wrong password"
findings.description: Unknown-email and wrong-password paths return distinct messages/codes (ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND vs INCORRECT_PASSWORD), letting an attacker enumerate registered emails.
findings.exploit_scenario: Scripted login attempts across an email wordlist partition registered vs unregistered addresses for phishing/credential-stuffing targeting.
findings.recommendation: Return an identical generic message/code for both cases; perform a dummy hash comparison on the unknown-email path.

findings.title: Access token returned in JSON response body in addition to the httpOnly cookie
findings.description: register/login handlers set the httpOnly cookie AND return accessToken in the JSON body (by design per an inline comment), which the frontend then stores in localStorage (see F-FE-02) — defeating the httpOnly protection.
findings.exploit_scenario: Same as F-FE-02: any XSS can read the token straight out of localStorage.
findings.recommendation: Stop returning accessToken in the response body for browser clients; rely solely on the cookie.

findings.title: jsonwebtoken pinned to old 8.5.1; jwt.verify() doesn't restrict algorithms
findings.description: Pinned before the 9.x line's algorithm-confusion hardening. Current usage is symmetric-only (HS256, static secret) with no exposed public key, so no concrete exploit chain today; risk is latent if the scheme is ever extended.
findings.exploit_scenario: No standalone exploit against current usage; risk materializes only if an asymmetric/JWKS verification path is added without an explicit algorithms allowlist.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to jsonwebtoken 9.x; pass { algorithms: ['HS256'] } explicitly to every jwt.verify() call.

findings.title: Registration endpoint reveals whether a specific email or phone is already registered
findings.description: The conflict check discloses exactly which field (email vs phone) collided.
findings.exploit_scenario: Submitting a target's email with an arbitrary phone confirms the target holds a PayFlow account.
findings.recommendation: Return a generic conflict message that doesn't indicate which field matched.
findings.note: Not one of the 18 numbered VULN branches — pre-existing baseline behavior surfaced by this scan, adjacent to VULN-009.

findings.title: Non-constant-time comparison of password hash digests
findings.description: verifyPassword compares digests with === rather than crypto.timingSafeEqual.
findings.exploit_scenario: Largely theoretical; network jitter dominates, and F-AUTH-01 is a far more direct attack path.
findings.recommendation: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual; subsumed by the F-AUTH-01 bcrypt/argon2id fix.
findings.note: Not one of the 18 numbered VULN branches — pre-existing baseline behavior, same class as the earlier standalone scan's F-005.

findings.title: Missing ownership check allows any authenticated user to delete another user's beneficiary (IDOR)
findings.description: deleteBeneficiary(_callerUserId, id) never uses _callerUserId; prisma.beneficiary.delete({ where: { id } }) has no ownerUserId filter, unlike listBeneficiaries/addBeneficiary in the same file.
findings.exploit_scenario: DELETE /beneficiaries/{victim-uuid} with any authenticated session deletes the victim's saved beneficiary.
findings.recommendation: Scope the delete by id AND ownerUserId; treat zero-row result as NotFoundError.
findings.note: Independently confirmed TRUE_POSITIVE by 3/3 adversarial /triage verifiers in a prior run — see backend/TRIAGE-vuln-002.json.

summary.coverage_note: 17/18 injected vulnerabilities directly surfaced (VULN-007 surfaced twice, once per vantage point: F-AUTH-05 backend + F-FE-02 frontend). VULN-006 (missing 2-decimal-place check on transfer amount) shares its schema line with VULN-005 after the branch merge; the scanner reported the positivity gap (F-XFER-01) but did not separately call out the precision gap. 3 additional low-confidence findings (F-AUTH-03, F-AUTH-06, and dependency finding F-MW-04) are pre-existing baseline patterns, not among the 18 planted vulns.
